title: Spectacles: A Verified Compiler from Semiring-Weighted Automata to Zero-Knowledge Scoring Circuits

reviewers.name: Yuan Cheng
reviewers.key_strength: The algebraic decomposition of NLP metrics into WFAs over explicitly chosen semirings provides unambiguous denotational semantics that the evaluation community has lacked.
reviewers.key_weakness: The PSI contamination detection operates under a semi-honest security model, which is inadequate for the adversarial setting the system claims to address.

reviewers.name: Aniruddha Sinha
reviewers.key_strength: The explicit threat model with honest acknowledgment of limitations (e.g., model identity substitution is out of scope) builds genuine trust in the claims that are made.
reviewers.key_weakness: The composition of STARK proofs, PSI protocol, and commitment scheme lacks mechanized verification—the most critical model checking opportunity is missed.

reviewers.name: Lila Zhang
reviewers.key_strength: The KleeneSemiring typeclass and verified WFA library in Lean 4 fill a recognized Mathlib gap and constitute a lasting contribution independent of the ZK application.
reviewers.key_weakness: WFA determinization and Hopcroft minimization correctness are classified as should-prove rather than must-prove, leaving the equivalence decision procedure—a headline contribution—potentially unverified.

reviewers.name: Sara Roy
reviewers.key_strength: The triple implementation of each metric with property-based differential testing via proptest is excellent ML-verification bridge engineering.
reviewers.key_weakness: The seven WFA-compatible metrics miss the evaluation methods that matter most for modern LLM evaluation (BERTScore, LLM-as-judge), limiting practical impact.

reviewers.name: Joseph S. Chang
reviewers.key_strength: The two-tier soundness architecture with generic algebraic compilation (proved once, instantiated per semiring) demonstrates exemplary parametric proof design.
reviewers.key_weakness: The gap between Lean 4 formalization and Rust implementation is bridged only by differential testing, not by verified extraction or refinement—the 'DeepSpec gap' limits end-to-end guarantees.

consensus_strengths: The WFA-over-semiring abstraction is mathematically clean and load-bearing—it simultaneously enables decidable equivalence, verified compilation, and efficient circuit synthesis.
The two-tier compilation architecture (algebraic for embeddable semirings, gadget-assisted for tropical) is intellectually honest and technically well-designed.
The Lean 4 formalization (KleeneSemiring typeclass, verified WFA library, two tactics) constitutes a lasting Mathlib contribution independent of the ZK application.
The threat model is explicit about what is and is not claimed, particularly the honest limitation regarding model identity substitution (A2).
consensus_weaknesses: The PSI contamination protocol assumes semi-honest adversaries, which contradicts the adversarial threat the system addresses; malicious-security PSI is needed.
The Lean-to-Rust trust boundary is bridged by differential testing rather than verified extraction, creating a gap in the end-to-end formal guarantee.
Coverage is limited to seven traditional NLP metrics, missing modern LLM evaluation methods (BERTScore, LLM-as-judge) where contamination concerns are most acute.

Key proof obligations (WFA determinization, Hopcroft minimization, wfa_equiv completeness) are classified as should-prove or deferred, undermining the equivalence decision procedure's headline contribution.
The composition security of STARK proofs with the PSI protocol lacks mechanized verification, relying only on a manual appeal to Canetti's sequential composition theorem.
actionable_recommendations: Upgrade the PSI protocol to malicious-security (e.g., using cut-and-choose or dual-execution techniques) or clearly document semi-honest as a limitation in the threat model summary.
Promote WFA determinization and Hopcroft minimization correctness from should-prove to must-prove, as they are load-bearing for the equivalence decision procedure headline contribution.
Add a TLA+ specification of the full composed protocol (STARK + PSI + commitment) to verify protocol interaction safety, not just the commit-reveal sub-protocol.
Provide a quantitative analysis of contamination threshold τ sensitivity, including the expected baseline n-gram overlap from the language's background distribution across languages.
Develop a roadmap for extending the WFA fragment to cover embedding-based metrics (BERTScore) or formally characterize the boundary of WFA-expressible evaluation functions.
